change: Version 0.1: first release with 13 cases, 34 official responses and 34 policy instruments across ASEAN, Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam and the Philippines. Every row has a source link and a confidence rating.
Method decision: any action by a government body or a person with official authority counts as a response (statements, warnings, advisories, investigations, orders, laws).

Version 0.2: added Thailand; 6 new cases (SG-I-05, TH-I-01 to TH-I-03, PH-I-03, PH-I-04), 8 new official responses and 9 new policies (6 Thailand, 1 Philippines, 2 ASEAN including DEFA, signed 14 Nov 2026). Added an aim_url column linking cases to their OECD AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor record. Added coverage and proof-of-concept notices.

Version 0.3: optional cookieless visitor counting with GoatCounter (off by default, nothing is added to the page unless a site code is set). New Visitors tab with a live total, a region view, a country table, referring sites, tab use and downloads, shown only after 30 visits and with groups under 3 merged. New fetch_stats.py and a daily GitHub workflow refresh the country snapshot. No cookies; nothing is counted for Do Not Track, Global Privacy Control or local files.

Template, 2026-11-23: the ASEAN emblem is no longer used; the non-affiliation statement is kept and the Method section explains this. Added a Back to top button and footer links, and a header link to AI Benar Advisory. The privacy notice link now points to its GitHub copy, so it works however the site is hosted. Map tiles: accessible names now start with their visible text (code, name, number) for voice-control users, hover tooltips are hidden from screen readers (the label carries the same details), and empty-tile names meet 4.5:1 contrast.

Version 0.5: a new Compute tab, on chips, data centres and verification. It records published data centre capacity by market (with what each figure measures), named projects, and rules, responses and cases about where AI chips go, including the US licence rule for Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia. It compares planned with running capacity using one firm's figures, shows a "Can it be checked?" profile of five questions for each member with no total or ranking, lists public signals to check when something is not in the news, and sets out the layers at which compute could be verified, with whose cooperation.

Method decision: investigations and charges about chips are recorded as reported, and every such row must say that an investigation is not a finding and a charge is an allegation until a court decides. The Compute tab does not name people.

Renamed from the ASEAN AI Governance Tracker to the ASEAN AI Governance and Safety Tracker, to reflect the new coverage of AI safety and compute. The web address is unchanged, so existing links keep working.

Easier to read: cities on the Compute tab now show their country (Johor, Malaysia), abbreviations and country codes are explained the first time they appear on each tab (hover, or tap on a phone), the Method tab lists them all, the Compute charts stay readable on phones, and links shared on social media show the tracker's name, description and an image.

Explanations for every short form and organisation that can be explained with confidence: 206 in all, including Malay, Indonesian, Vietnamese and Portuguese names. A line under the tabs says how to see them (hover, or tap on a phone), and the Method tab lists them all. Where a short form has two meanings in the tracker, both are given. A few are left unexplained until they can be confirmed.
Restored two automatic checks that were missing from the repository: the review checklist on each pull request (see REVIEWING.md), and the check that the page matches its template.

Version 0.6: renamed the ASEAN AI Governance and Safety Tracker; 206 short forms and organisations explained; cities shown with their country on the Compute tab; the tracker's name and logo return to its starting view, and the AI Benar home link leads to the AI Benar home page. No data changed.
